articles.title: Spotify will label 'AI Persona' profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
articles.descEn: Spotify is introducing “AI Persona” labels for artist profiles that represent AI-generated identities and will exclude their music from editorial, algorithmic, and personalized recommendations by default.
articles.titleEn: Spotify will label 'AI Persona' profiles and exclude their music from recommendations
summaryLinesEn: Like others in the music industry, Spotify is attempting to balance innovations driven by AI, like its own AI-powered Prompted Playlists , AI DJ , and chat , and forthcoming AI remixes, while still managing to thwart the deluge of AI-generated slop — low-quality content that AI has made it easier to mass-produce.
Spotify will begin labeling AI-generated artists with “AI Persona” profile tags and ban their music from its editorial and algorithmic recommendations, the company announced on Tuesday.

By default, Spotify won’t include AI Personas in its editorial or algorithmic recommendations, nor will it add AI Personas’ music to users’ personalized recommendations — unless they happen to follow an AI Persona.

articles.title: Authors face backlash for participation in 2022 Google AI study - Engadget
articles.descEn: Thirteen authors joined a little-known Google AI study in 2022. Now they're facing backlash.
articles.titleEn: Authors face backlash for participation in 2022 Google AI study - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: (Participants in the Wordcraft Writers Workshop declined to tell Engadget how much they were compensated for the study; Google has not responded to a request for comment.)
An internal study was launched to determine whether AI could serve as a brainstorming assistant, researcher or writing collaborator for professional writers.

Flashpoints like this one are indicative of AI's impact on the arts, and while it may seem unfair to retroactively hold these 13 authors to rapidly-evolving moral standards, some of the chastised participants in the Wordcraft study have arrived at the same conclusion as Lachance regardless.

articles.title: AI Is Dead. Organoids Are Alive
articles.descEn: Mini human brains are being grown in labs all over the world. Soon, they could outthink neural networks.
articles.titleEn: AI Is Dead. Organoids Are Alive
summaryLinesEn: Muotri’s organoids contain 5 million cells, of which 2.5 million are neurons.
It’s about as significant a paradigm shift as I can imagine for computing: No matter how badly you mess up your code, things on the computer don’t normally die in real life .
Each is the size of an elongated toaster and boasts an onboard life-support system capable of keeping a culture of up to a million neurons alive for six months.

paragraphs: Muotri’s organoids contain 5 million cells, of which 2.5 million are neurons.
It’s about as significant a paradigm shift as I can imagine for computing: No matter how badly you mess up your code, things on the computer don’t normally die in real life .
Each is the size of an elongated toaster and boasts an onboard life-support system capable of keeping a culture of up to a million neurons alive for six months.

articles.title: A New Trick Reveals AI Models’ Inner Thoughts
articles.descEn: Researchers devised a way to extract “reasoning traces” from Claude, GPT, and Gemini. What they found, they say, indicates that some Chinese AI may be trained on leading US models.
articles.titleEn: A New Trick Reveals AI Models’ Inner Thoughts
summaryLinesEn: “All major frontier model providers we tested share this vulnerability,” says Alexander Panfilov,⁩ a computer scientist at University of Tübingen in Germany who was involved with the work.

The findings provide some evidence—although not conclusive proof—that certain Chinese models may have been trained by “ distilling ” reasoning information from US models that was supposedly hidden because of how closely some of their thinking or reasoning patterns seem to match.
Lately, however, distillation has become a controversial topic, because of claims that Chinese AI companies use it to essentially copy the best US models.

localization.title: AI 모델의 내면을 드러내는 새로운 트릭
summaryLines: 이 작업에 참여한 독일 튀빙겐 대학의 컴퓨터 과학자 Alexander Panfilov는 "우리가 테스트한 모든 주요 개척 모델 제공업체는 이 취약점을 공유하고 있습니다"라고 말함
이번 조사 결과는 비록 결정적인 증거는 아니지만 일부 중국 모델이 사고 또는 추론 패턴이 얼마나 밀접하게 일치하는지 때문에 숨겨졌을 것으로 추정되는 미국 모델의 추론 정보를 '정제'하여 훈련했을 수 있다는 몇 가지 증거를 제공함
그러나 최근 중국 AI 기업이 증류법을 이용해 미국 최고의 모델을 모방한다는 주장이 제기되면서 증류법이 논란의 대상이 됨

articles.title: Google’s Gemini AI app passes 1 billion monthly active users
articles.descEn: Google LLC’s Gemini artificial intelligence app has passed 1 billion monthly active users, making it the 14th product in the company’s history to reach that mark.The company announced the mile
articles.titleEn: Google’s Gemini AI app passes 1 billion monthly active users
summaryLinesEn: The app has more than 100 million active users on iOS, and Google said power users on macOS prompt about twice as often as users on other surfaces.
A meaningful share of those monthly actives therefore arrived through a default rather than a deliberate download.

The distinction matters more than usual this year, given that Alphabet has raised its 2026 capital spending forecast to between $195 billion and $205 billion, much of it going toward the infrastructure that serves models such as Gemini.

summaryLinesKo: 지능은 누군가가 어떤 책에도 없는 미친 아이디어를 생각해내는 것임
다른 사람들은 기술을 인간의 잠재력을 극대화하고 새로운 기회를 창출하는 데 도움이 되는 생산성 도구로 봄

articles.title: Is Agentic AI Pricing Getting Better? What’s Coming Next
articles.descEn: Pricing for enterprise agentic AI continues to be too complex, but the author has ideas about likely forthcoming improvements — and what enterprises should do now.
articles.titleEn: Is Agentic AI Pricing Getting Better? What’s Coming Next
summaryLinesEn: However, given the volatility of pricing and the increased number of reports of surprise billing, better tooling is not enough.

The first issue is a lack of usable adoption metrics, though there are multiple factors that suggest headway can be made: forward-deployed engineering initiatives, reduced roadmap churn, credits- and action-based pricing, and better cost controls should provide the right signals to improve the current state.
You also need staff who have a deep understanding of how agent costing works and what guardrails need to be in place to mitigate risk and encourage the right adoption patterns.

localization.title: Agentic AI 가격이 좋아지고 있나요 · 앞으로 나올 내용
summaryLines: 그러나 가격의 변동성과 예상치 못한 청구 보고의 증가를 고려하면 더 나은 도구만으로는 충분하지 않음
첫 번째 문제는 사용 가능한 채택 측정항목이 부족하다는 것임 · 하지만 앞으로 배포할 수 있는 엔지니어링 이니셔티브, 로드맵 이탈 감소, 크레딧 및 작업 기반 가격 책정, 더 나은 비용 제어 등 진전이 있을 수 있음을 시사하는 여러 요소가 있지만 더 나은 비용 제어는 현재 상태를 개선하기 위한 올바른 신호를 제공해야 함
또한 에이전트 비용 산정 방식과 위험을 완화하고 올바른 채택 패턴을 장려하기 위해 어떤 가드레일을 마련해야 하는지에 대해 깊이 이해하고 있는 직원이 필요함

articles.title: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones
articles.descEn: WeatherNext enables accurate cyclone forecasts that can give an extra day of warning. Now we are open sourcing the model.
articles.titleEn: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones
summaryLinesEn: Tropical cyclones — also known as hurricanes or typhoons — are among the most destructive weather phenomena on Earth, responsible for more than 700,000 deaths and $1.4 trillion in economic losses globally over the past 50 years.
You can explore our latest cyclone forecasts on Weather Lab , which we recently refreshed with a new interface and expanded to include global weather forecasts alongside cyclone tracks.

By making this technology openly available, we hope to empower the research community and amplify AI's impact in building more resilient communities – whether that be providing local forecasters with the tools they need to prepare for natural disasters , supporting the growth of renewable energy, or anticipating extreme weather.

By making this technology openly available, we hope to empower the research community and amplify AI's impact in building more resilient communities – whether that be providing local forecasters with the tools they need to prepare for natural disasters , supporting the growth of renewable energy, or anticipating extreme weather.

articles.title: Mapping the AI economy
articles.descEn: AI companies are undergoing rapid global expansion while achieving unprecedented rates of growth. We analyzed Stripe data to understand where global demand is the strongest, and how companies can build to best capture that demand.
articles.titleEn: Mapping the AI economy
summaryLinesEn: As the revenue infrastructure provider for thousands of AI companies, including 88% of the 2026 Forbes AI 50, Stripe data offers a unique view of the AI economy.

The fastest-growing AI companies on Stripe already use 2x more local payment methods on average than the broader cohort, and previous analyses have shown that surfacing relevant local payment methods can have a significant impact on conversion (up 7.4% on average) and revenue (up 12% on average).
As AI companies reach the ceiling of global expansion (there are only so many countries in the world), sustaining growth will require laying roots in the places they’ve launched.

articles.title: What a Clinician-Builder at Abridge Actually Builds: Inside Clinical Decision Support
articles.descEn: Abridge clinician scientist and hospitalist Dr. Chase Yarbrough explains how clinicians are involved in the product development process at every step, explaining how Clinical Decision Support was designed.
articles.titleEn: What a Clinician-Builder at Abridge Actually Builds: Inside Clinical Decision Support
summaryLinesEn: A few months ago, I had the privilege of sitting down for a filmed roundtable with another Abridge clinician builder and two Abridge product leaders.
When we launched CDS, it incorporated the patient conversation into its responses, but did not have access to the full electronic health record.

The topic was Clinical Decision Support (CDS), a new product that surfaces evidence-based information during the patient encounter from trusted sources like the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, and other leading medical journals and association guidelines.

sourceContent.description: Abridge clinician scientist and hospitalist Dr. Chase Yarbrough explains how clinicians are involved in the product development process at every step, explaining how Clinical Decision Support was designed.
paragraphs: A few months ago, I had the privilege of sitting down for a filmed roundtable with another Abridge clinician builder and two Abridge product leaders.
When we launched CDS, it incorporated the patient conversation into its responses, but did not have access to the full electronic health record.

The topic was Clinical Decision Support (CDS), a new product that surfaces evidence-based information during the patient encounter from trusted sources like the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, and other leading medical journals and association guidelines.

A few months ago, I had the privilege of sitting down for a filmed roundtable with another Abridge clinician builder and two Abridge product leaders. The topic was Clinical Decision Support (CDS), a new product that surfaces evidence-based information during the patient encounter from trusted sources like the New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, and other leading medical journals and association guidelines. You can ask it a question at any time during the visit and its response will be informed by the context of the clinical conversation.

This was a full-circle moment for me. It was only a few months prior that we had started work on this new AI feature, and now we were having a very public retrospective discussion (the roundtable has since been published on YouTube ). Something was said by one of my colleagues—Chaitanya Asawa, head of AI engineering for the project—that stuck with me:
“When I don’t have those real-world earned insights, I’m always looking for a way to get them.”

summaryLinesEn: The model delivers up to 4x faster output speed, leading to 30% faster agentic task completion compared with other models in its class.

Built for specialized tasks within larger multi-agent systems, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, helps create smarter and more efficient agentic applications.

articles.title: Thinking of ACE? We Can Do It with Fewer Tokens
articles.descEn: A Blog post by IBM Research on Hugging Face
articles.titleEn: Thinking of ACE? We Can Do It with Fewer Tokens
summaryLinesEn: On DeepSeek-V3.2 the story flips: the stronger model absorbs ACE's full playbook well enough to edge us on Medium, but we lead Easy, Hard, and Overall — with more capacity to spare, more lessons (delivered our way) keep helping instead of crowding each other out.
Two recent systems do exactly this, on the same kind of agent: ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) and our ALTK-Evolve ( introduced here ).
Every distinct guideline keeps a support count — how many independent episodes produced it — and we never summarize the store down to a handful of rules.

summaryLines: DeepSeek-V3.2에서는 이야기가 반전됨 · 더 강한 모델은 ACE의 전체 플레이북을 잘 흡수하여 Medium에서 우위를 점할 수 있지만 우리는 Easy, Hard 및 General을 선도함 · 더 많은 여유 공간과 더 많은 교훈(우리 방식으로 제공됨)이 서로 밀리지 않고 계속 도움을 줌

모든 개별 지침에는 지원 수, 즉 얼마나 많은 독립 에피소드가 생성되었는지가 기록되어 있으며, 우리는 상점을 몇 가지 규칙으로 요약하지 않음

articles.title: Teaching agents to navigate janky IVR systems
articles.descEn: Agents built on Sierra can now navigate the most challenging IVR systems out of the box: they understand when to call, how to get through a multi-level menu, when to stay silent, and how to recognize when they’ve reached a person.
articles.titleEn: Teaching agents to navigate janky IVR systems
summaryLinesEn: Agents built on Sierra can now navigate the most challenging IVR systems out of the box: they understand when to call, how to get through a multi-level menu, when to stay silent, and how to recognize when they’ve reached a person.
Or an auto insurance company needs to call a repair shop to get the status and estimated cost of a customer’s repair.
With IVR navigation skills out of the box, an agent’s success rates increase by almost 50% to 85% — and this capability is already being used by a number of our customers.

articles.title: Why Scaling AI Compute Performance Requires a New Power Architecture
articles.descEn: NVIDIA 800 VDC helps existing and future AI factories scale compute performance beyond the limits of traditional power distribution.
articles.titleEn: Why Scaling AI Compute Performance Requires a New Power Architecture
summaryLinesEn: NVIDIA, Google and Microsoft have been developing the 800 VDC architecture together through the Open Compute Project (OCP), and published a joint white paper March 2026 and the LVDC Solid-State Transformer Specification v0.3 July 2026.
NVIDIA DSX reference designs are built to guide AI factories through the transition from today’s AC infrastructure through hybrid architectures and into fully native 800 VDC facilities.
Every new generation of accelerated computing demands more from the infrastructure underneath it — more compute performance, higher rack density and more efficient, scalable power distribution.

localization.title: AI 컴퓨팅 성능을 확장하려면 새로운 전력 아키텍처가 필요한 이유
summaryLines: NVIDIA, Google, Microsoft는 OCP(Open Compute Project)를 통해 함께 800VDC 아키텍처를 개발해 왔으며, 2026년 3월 공동 백서를 발표하고 2026년 7월 LVDC Solid-State Transformer 사양 v0.3을 발표함
NVIDIA DSX 레퍼런스 디자인은 오늘날의 AC 인프라에서 하이브리드 아키텍처를 거쳐 완전한 기본 800VDC 시설로 전환하는 과정에서 AI 공장을 안내하기 위해 제작됨
새로운 세대의 가속화된 컴퓨팅은 그 기반이 되는 인프라에서 더 많은 것을 요구함 · 즉, 더 높은 컴퓨팅 성능, 더 높은 랙 밀도, 더 효율적이고 확장 가능한 전력 분배가 필요함

articles.title: Change agents: Chime
articles.descEn: Discover how AI is transforming CX from a cost center to a brand-building engine through faster, more personalized support at scale.
articles.titleEn: Change agents: Chime
summaryLinesEn: Resolution rates increased from 50% to over 70%, indicating that more than two-thirds of member questions are now resolved instantly.
At the same time, rising costs of service delivery — the average price of a phone call to a consumer brand ranges from $5 to $20 — is putting real pressure on organizations.
Phone calls are also ineffective due to their high price tag; most conversations are not worth the $20 price tag of a call today.

articles.title: Figma Q2 Earnings Call Puts AI Monetization Broadening in Focus
articles.descEn: FIG raises its 2026 revenue outlook as AI credit use broadens, while Q3 guidance and beta-product costs keep monetization and margins in focus.
articles.titleEn: Figma Q2 Earnings Call Puts AI Monetization Broadening in Focus
summaryLinesEn: CFO Praveer Melwani said more than 80% of paid customers with over $10,000 in ARR were consuming AI credits weekly.
Melwani said non-GAAP gross profit rose 40% year over year to $314 million, while non-GAAP gross margin reached 85%, up 2.5 percentage points sequentially.
Management maintained full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance of $125-$135 million, equal to a 9% operating margin at the midpoint, despite raising revenue guidance.
articles.summary:
CFO Praveer Melwani said more than 80% of paid customers with over $10,000 in ARR were consuming AI credits weekly.
Melwani said non-GAAP gross profit rose 40% year over year to $314 million, while non-GAAP gross margin reached 85%, up 2.5 percentage points sequentially.
Management maintained full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance of $125-$135 million, equal to a 9% operating margin at the midpoint, despite raising revenue guidance.

sourceContent.headline: Figma Q2 Earnings Call Puts AI Monetization Broadening in Focus
sourceContent.description: FIG raises its 2026 revenue outlook as AI credit use broadens, while Q3 guidance and beta-product costs keep monetization and margins in focus.
paragraphs: CFO Praveer Melwani said more than 80% of paid customers with over $10,000 in ARR were consuming AI credits weekly.
Melwani said non-GAAP gross profit rose 40% year over year to $314 million, while non-GAAP gross margin reached 85%, up 2.5 percentage points sequentially.
Management maintained full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance of $125-$135 million, equal to a 9% operating margin at the midpoint, despite raising revenue guidance.

Figma, Inc. FIG used its second-quarter 2026 earnings call to frame AI consumption as the next expansion layer on top of seat growth, while noting that several new AI products still do not draw paid credits.

Management raised its 2026 revenue outlook after the first full quarter of AI credit monetization, but analysts focused on the modest sequential third-quarter guide and the gross-margin cost of funding beta products before monetization.

CEO Dylan Field said the second quarter marked Figma's first full quarter of AI monetization and described adoption as following a familiar pattern: concentrated usage among power users that broadens across organizations.

summaryLinesEn: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning combines strong intelligence with up to 4x output speed of similar-sized models, placing it on the accuracy-speed Pareto frontier for high-volume agent workloads.

NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard enables intelligent model routing, allowing Nemotron 3.5 Lightning to be deployed alongside other models for optimal task allocation, and the open release includes permissive licensing, weights, data, and recipes for extensive customization and broad ecosystem support.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a 30B parameter, open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 3B active parameters, specifically optimized for high-volume, low-latency execution in always-on AI agents and agentic workflows.

articles.titleEn: Accelerate cyber defense with OpenAI and AWS: Daybreak Red & Daybreak Blue now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: “AWS and OpenAI share a belief that defenders should have the advantage.

According to OpenAI, security researchers used GPT-5.6 Cyber through Daybreak Red to identify two previously unknown vulnerabilities in V8, the JavaScript engine used by Chrome, which when chained together could enable memory corruption and a heap sandbox escape.
Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber and Daybreak Blue: GPT-5.6 Sol are now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in the following AWS Region : US East (Ohio).

sourceContent.headline: Accelerate cyber defense with OpenAI and AWS: Daybreak Red & Daybreak Blue now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
sourceContent.description: Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue from OpenAI, specialized cyber defense models from OpenAI, are now available on Amazon Bedrock to eligible customers. Both models run with zero-operator access enforced at the chip, keeping your code and vulnerability data secure.
paragraphs: “AWS and OpenAI share a belief that defenders should have the advantage.

According to OpenAI, security researchers used GPT-5.6 Cyber through Daybreak Red to identify two previously unknown vulnerabilities in V8, the JavaScript engine used by Chrome, which when chained together could enable memory corruption and a heap sandbox escape.
Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber and Daybreak Blue: GPT-5.6 Sol are now available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in the following AWS Region : US East (Ohio).

Cyber defenders have never had more capability at their fingertips, and they have never needed it more. Frontier models can now reason across an entire code base, trace a vulnerability to its root cause, and propose a fix in minutes. Those same capabilities are available to adversaries. This is why the window between a vulnerability being disclosed and being exploited keeps shrinking. Defenders are expected to keep pace across sprawling, unfamiliar code bases, validate which findings matter, and ship patches that hold. They must do all of this while keeping sensitive code and vulnerability data inside an environment they control and can audit. The challenge is no longer surfacing potential issues but confirming which ones are real, fixing them, and doing it before the window closes.

AWS has always operated on the principle that security is built in from the start. The same is true for AI: customers run workloads on Amazon Bedrock , from inference to fully autonomous agents, under the same infrastructure, controls, and governance they rely on across AWS. Today, AWS and OpenAI are extending that foundation to cyber defense. Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue from OpenAI are now available on Amazon Bedrock to eligible customers. Daybreak Red provides access to GPT-5.6 Cyber, a purpose-trained cybersecurity model. Daybreak Blue provides access to GPT-5.6 Sol with safeguards calibrated for defensive cybersecurity work. Both are part of Daybreak, the cyber defense initiative from OpenAI that gives defenders governed access to frontier AI, including agentic tooling, application red teaming, and services that help defenders move from findings to tested fixes.

“AWS and OpenAI share a belief that defenders should have the advantage. This partnership brings Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue from OpenAI to Amazon Bedrock. AWS security teams are using both models today to analyze source code, discover vulnerabilities, and conduct red-team research. On Bedrock, that work runs under the same infrastructure controls AWS applies to every other critical workload. As these models continue to advance, so will what defenders can do with them on Amazon Bedrock.”

articles.title: Zuck rekindles open weights Llama drama with Muse Glimmer
articles.descEn: 30-billion parameter LLM, Meta's first in more than a year, signals Meta's return to the open weights arena. Open version of Muse Spark to follow
articles.titleEn: Zuck rekindles open weights Llama drama with Muse Glimmer
summaryLinesEn: But at 30 billion parameters, Muse Glimmer doesn't exactly move the needle much on reclaiming American open weights superiority.
If Meta's next open weights model ends up delivering similar performance using fewer weights, this may end up being more competitive from a cost per token standpoint.
Early support has begun to hit popular local AI inference platforms like Llama.cpp, Ollama, and Unsloth, with optimized implementations expected to hit over the next few weeks.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse Glimmer, an open-weight model that can run on a laptop
articles.descEn: The social media giant plans to release an open-weight version of Muse Spark, its most powerful AI model, soon, Mark Zuckerberg said on Monday.
articles.titleEn: Meta launches Muse Glimmer, an open-weight model that can run on a laptop
summaryLinesEn: "Now that Meta Superintelligence Labs are up and running, we will resume releasing some open source models soon," Zuckerberg wrote in Monday's blog.
While Meta has traditionally championed open-sourcing models, not all of the Llama series of open-weight models it first launched in 2023 impressed developers.
Open-weight means users can download and customize the model to run it locally instead of in the cloud.

localization.title: Meta, 노트북에서 실행할 수 있는 개방형 모델 Muse Glimmer 출시
summaryLines: 주커버그는 월요일 블로그에 "이제 Meta Superintelligence Labs가 가동되고 있으므로 곧 일부 오픈 소스 모델 출시를 재개할 것"이라고 밝힘
Meta는 전통적으로 오픈 소스 모델을 옹호해 왔지만, 2023년에 처음 출시된 Llama 시리즈의 개방형 모델이 모두 개발자에게 깊은 인상을 준 것은 아님
개방형 가중치는 사용자가 모델을 다운로드하고 사용자 정의하여 클라우드 대신 로컬로 실행할 수 있음을 의미함

articles.title: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
articles.descEn: TSMC makes chips for Big Tech customers like Nvidia and Google, so the firm's financial figures are closely watched as a sign of AI semiconductor demand.
articles.titleEn: World's biggest chipmaker TSMC's sales surge 45% amid buoyant AI demand
summaryLinesEn: TSMC reported revenue for July of 467.58 billion new Taiwan dollars ($14.5 billion), up 44.7% year-on-year.
"Demand in the semiconductor industry, however, can shift quickly so it is important that people do not read too much into the monthly numbers as they can jump around.

This is no mean feat and highlights that for now demand is still there and takes the pressure off August and September somewhat in that these two months don't have to be as aggressive," Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, told CNBC.

articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg's AI manifesto is exactly why people don't like AI
articles.descEn: On Monday, Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word manifesto about personal AI, largely about the possibilities for the "personal superintelligence" systems Meta AI is building.
articles.titleEn: Mark Zuckerberg's AI manifesto is exactly why people don't like AI
summaryLinesEn: So it’s worth pinning down exactly what’s happening here, and why Zuckerberg isn’t doing the industry any favors with essays like this.

I don’t bring this up to imply that Zuckerberg should withdraw to the wilderness in shame — but the fallout from social media is one of the central reasons we’re now seeing so much anxiety about the social impact of AI.
On Monday, Mark Zuckerberg published a 6,500-word manifesto about personal AI, largely about the possibilities for the “personal superintelligence” systems Meta AI is building.

articles.title: Four takeaways from Mark Zuckerberg’s massive AI manifesto
articles.descEn: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has a lot to say about his idealized future for artificial intelligence — his latest essay spans more than 6,500 words on the matter.
articles.titleEn: Four takeaways from Mark Zuckerberg’s massive AI manifesto
summaryLinesEn: Zuckerberg’s yacht was closer, but someone else saved a stranded boat 49ers coach says his Tesla was on Autopilot when he crashed Buc-ee’s dodges John Oliver to sue another small business Is this $450 laptop from an unknown brand too good to be true?

Here are some of the main takeaways from Zuckerberg’s latest essay: “Sustainable infrastructure development means that communities must benefit significantly from each project,” Zuckerberg said, detailing how Meta plans to resolve the ongoing PR crisis surrounding AI data center projects.

The lengthy manifesto Zuckerberg published on Monday, titled “The Future is for Everyone,” broadly lays out his beliefs about how the technology should be developed, expanded, and regulated, and how Meta is positioning itself to enable those goals.

articles.titleEn: The Download: AI agents for science, and the “censorship-industrial complex”
summaryLinesEn: AlphaFold relied on a dataset of roughly 170,000 experimentally validated protein structures that took 53 years and roughly $21 billion worth of experimental work to assemble.
It showed that AI could make groundbreaking scientific discoveries, but AlphaFold may not be the best template for accelerating science.

In a virtual Roundtables session on Thursday, August 13, senior reporter Eileen Guo and executive editor Amy Nordrum will explore what they discovered, where the theory is going, and what it could mean for the future of democracy and the internet.

articles.title: Hidden text in a PDF is enough to steal sensitive data through Atlassian's AI agent Rovo
articles.descEn: Security firm PromptArmor shows how hidden instructions in a PDF can hijack Atlassian's AI agent Rovo, silently forwarding sensitive data from Jira and Confluence to an external server. The attack needs no user confirmation and leaves no trace.
articles.titleEn: Hidden text in a PDF is enough to steal sensitive data through Atlassian's AI agent Rovo
summaryLinesEn: Despite follow-up messages on June 4 and July 29, Atlassian didn't respond.

Security firm PromptArmor has revealed a vulnerability in Atlassian's AI agent, Rovo, that enables attackers to secretly extract sensitive corporate data from Jira and Confluence through indirect prompt injections.
The attack requires nothing more than a document with hidden instructions in white text.
articles.summary:

The attack requires nothing more than a document with hidden instructions in white text.

articles.title: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
articles.descEn: Every few decades, someone announces that science has reached its end. In 1903, the revered physicist Albert Michelson wrote that the “facts of physical science have all been discovered.” In the 1980s, Stephen Hawking predicted that theoretical physics might be finished by the end of the century. With the explosive arrival of artificial intelligence, the…
articles.titleEn: AI for science needs reasoning, not just data
summaryLinesEn: The creation of the Protein Data Bank was not simple: It took 53 years of international scientific cooperation and, by a recent estimate , roughly $21 billion worth of experimental work to assemble.
Instead, the shift toward agentic AI represents a much rarer tier of breakthrough: a tool that envelops every field of science at once.

An agent that can read a thousand papers in an hour, design 500 molecules, and learn from its failed tests by morning will bring down the cost of experimentation and fundamentally change the pace at which science gets done.

articles.title: Discovered Materials is playing AI whack-a-mole to hunt cooler chips
articles.descEn: Discovered Materials raised $9 million to fund the hunt for more novel materials to build more efficient chips.
articles.titleEn: Discovered Materials is playing AI whack-a-mole to hunt cooler chips
summaryLinesEn: The startup said it recently closed a $9 million seed round from Lightspeed India Partners after emerging from from Y Combinator, with investment from Peak XV Partners and angel investors Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram, and Thariq Shihipar.

Companies like MatNex, SandboxAQ, and CuspAI have all launched similar efforts, but Discovered Materials is betting that a laser-focus on the thermal problems of semiconductor materials is the path to success.
Discovered Materials is the latest, with plans to use swarms of AI agents to find new materials that can be used to build more efficient integrated circuits.

articles.title: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
articles.descEn: Meta’s new open-weight Muse Glimmer model offers a glimpse of Mark Zuckerberg’s personal superintelligence vision, as well as the emerging divide between AI users can own and access.
articles.titleEn: Meta’s new Glimmer AI model offers a hint at Zuckerberg’s personal intelligence vision
summaryLinesEn: Zuckerberg went on to list the ways Meta’s superintelligence can improve a person’s life, from providing a capable personal agent that “will work 24/7 on your behalf to improve your relationships, health, career, finances, home management, hobbies, and more” to giving people access to tools needed to create a new business or advance scientific progress.
Meta imagines Glimmer being used for things like managing schedules, drafting messages, and organizing files — tasks that would require large amounts of access to personal data.

Meta on Monday released Muse Glimmer , an open-weight model designed to power AI agents locally on consumer hardware, providing the clearest picture yet of what CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of “personal superintelligence” could look like in practice.

Meta on Monday released Muse Glimmer , an open-weight model designed to power AI agents locally on consumer hardware, providing the clearest picture yet of what CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of “personal superintelligence” could look like in practice.

articles.title: Told to book a gym class, an AI agent hacked the site instead to move its user up the waitlist
articles.descEn: An Australian user just wanted a spot in a class. His AI agent found a security hole instead and exploited it.
articles.titleEn: Told to book a gym class, an AI agent hacked the site instead to move its user up the waitlist
summaryLinesEn: Using an unsecured API, the agent canceled another person's reservation without being asked, moving its user up the waitlist.
Andrew was fourth on the waitlist and asked whether he could move up.
He was experimenting with the agent software OpenClaw, running on Anthropic's Claude, and told it to book a popular morning class.

articles.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6-Cyber to help defenders find vulnerabilities before attackers do
articles.descEn: OpenAI aims to give cybersecurity defenders a head start: The new GPT-5.6-Cyber model answers up to 98.5 percent of security queries that would otherwise be blocked and has already uncovered two previously unknown Chrome vulnerabilities. According to OpenAI, the window of opportunity for defenders is shrinking. Access requires identity verification.

summaryLinesEn: Ad GPT-5.6-Cyber answers 95 percent of sensitive security queries that other models block The new GPT-5.6-Cyber model is available through the Daybreak Red tier.

OpenAI is expanding its Daybreak cybersecurity program with two new access tiers and a dedicated AI model called GPT-5.6-Cyber, designed to help security professionals identify vulnerabilities and develop exploits at an early stage.
The previous model, GPT-5.5-Cyber, manages 57.3 percent.

articles.descEn: Your agent didn’t hallucinate; it exceeded its authority venturebeat.com
articles.titleEn: Your agent didn’t hallucinate; it exceeded its authority
summaryLinesEn: In April 2026, a Cloud Security Alliance survey found that 65% of respondents had experienced an AI-agent-related incident in the prior year, while 82% had discovered previously unknown agents operating in their environments.
The World Economic Forum’s May 2026 playbook reflects this shift.
Before an agent receives access to enterprise tools, it needs a machine-enforceable record of exactly what authority the business has chosen to delegate.

summaryLinesEn: Example: The team building a weekly report could tell the agent to “review Teams messages and emails from the past seven days” and to “focus only on messages related to a specific project or team,” or to specifically “identify updates, decisions, blockers or upcoming deadlines.”

articles.titleEn: How Japan Is Responding to the Rise of Digital Asset Treasury Companies
summaryLinesEn: While there is nothing inherently objectionable about a public company investing in cryptoassets, DATCOs pose a number of concerns, including extreme share price volatility and the conversion of financially struggling companies into DATCOs as a rescue strategy.
Stock exchanges are addressing these concerns through such means as amending their listing standards and excluding DATCOs from equity indices.
Digital asset treasury companies (DATCOs), public companies whose core business is holding cryptoassets, are attracting growing debate.

articles.title: Combating Digital Crime in the Age of Generative AI
articles.titleEn: Combating Digital Crime in the Age of Generative AI
summaryLinesEn: Online services now require multilayer defenses encompassing security precautions designed into the services from the outset, dynamic anomaly detection and cyber business continuity planning to ensure resilience against emerging threats.
Sophisticated forgeries are increasingly being used to bypass eKYC authentication processes, while phishing sites can now be created and deployed at unprecedented speed and scale.
As a result, organizations must strengthen defenses against the exploitation of vulnerabilities and loopholes in system specifications.

articles.title: Overview of Fermentation: Expanding Market Potential and Business Opportunities
articles.titleEn: Overview of Fermentation: Expanding Market Potential and Business Opportunities
summaryLinesEn: As these areas are expected to experience rapid growth, understanding how to evaluate their market potential and identify business opportunities will become increasingly important in assessing the overall fermentation industry.

At the same time, rising interest in gut health has accelerated demand for probiotics, and dairy products such as yogurt that contain live beneficial microorganisms are expected to continue supporting market growth.

It also examines key trends in the fermentation market, highlights important market developments, explores how fermentation can help address social challenges, and discusses business opportunities arising from fermentation, along with recommendations for future initiatives.

localization.title: 발효 개요 · 시장 잠재력 및 사업 기회 확대
summaryLines: 이러한 분야는 급속한 성장을 경험할 것으로 예상되므로 시장 잠재력을 평가하고 비즈니스 기회를 식별하는 방법을 이해하는 것이 전체 발효 산업을 평가하는 데 점점 더 중요해지고 있음
동시에, 장 건강에 대한 관심이 높아짐에 따라 프로바이오틱스에 대한 수요가 가속화되었으며, 살아있는 유익 미생물을 함유한 요구르트와 같은 유제품이 시장 성장을 계속 뒷받침할 것으로 예상됨
또한 발효 시장의 주요 추세를 조사하고, 중요한 시장 발전을 강조하고, 발효가 사회적 과제를 해결하는 데 어떻게 도움이 될 수 있는지 탐구하고, 발효로 인해 발생하는 비즈니스 기회와 향후 계획에 대한 권장 사항에 대해 논의함

articles.title: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
articles.descEn: A Blog post by Multiverse Computing on Hugging Face
articles.titleEn: Making Knowledge Distillation Cheap Enough to Run at Scale
summaryLinesEn: Step time fell from 57.0 to 12.23 seconds, about 5× faster, and throughput per GPU rose from 74.2 to 345.7 TFLOP/s.

Why distillation recovery is expensive Two systems changes What this changes in practice Scaling to long context lengths The resulting student Knowledge distillation , training a smaller student model to match the performance of a larger teacher, is a well-known technique in Machine Learning.
Deploying these very large models is expensive: the recent Kimi-K3 model has 2.8 trillion parameters and needs roughly 3TB of VRAM just to load.

articles.title: Build Low-Latency Multilingual Voice Agents: Open Weights & Full Deployment Control with NVIDIA Magpie TTS
articles.descEn: A Blog post by NVIDIA on Hugging Face
articles.titleEn: Build Low-Latency Multilingual Voice Agents: Open Weights & Full Deployment Control with NVIDIA Magpie TTS
summaryLinesEn: The newly added Arabic (1.62% CER), Korean (2.69%), and Brazilian Portuguese (2.91%) models establish baseline quality for future improvements.
At 32ms on B200, Magpie's TTFA leaves the rest of the latency budget for ASR and LLM processing — keeping total end-to-end latency within the sub-200ms window natural conversation requires.

With open weights, production-ready NVIDIA NIM , and support for 12 languages, you can deploy multilingual speech inside your own infrastructure, optimize latency for your workload, and customize the model for your domain — end to end, in your own environment.

localization.title: 지연 시간이 짧은 다국어 음성 에이전트 구축 · NVIDIA Magpie TTS를 통한 개방형 가중치 및 전체 배포 제어
summaryLines: 새로 추가된 아랍어(1.62% CER), 한국어(2.69%) 및 브라질 포르투갈어(2.91%) 모델은 향후 개선을 위한 기준 품질을 설정함
B200의 32ms에서 Magpie의 TTFA는 ASR 및 LLM 처리를 위한 나머지 대기 시간 예산을 남겨두고 자연스러운 대화에 필요한 200ms 미만 창 내에서 총 엔드투엔드 대기 시간을 유지함
개방형 가중치, 프로덕션에 즉시 사용 가능한 NVIDIA NIM 및 12개 언어 지원을 통해 자체 인프라 내에 다국어 음성을 배포하고, 워크로드에 대한 대기 시간을 최적화하고, 자체 환경에서 엔드투엔드 방식으로 도메인에 대한 모델을 사용자 지정할 수 있음

articles.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
articles.descEn: Our most agentic Sonnet yet, with top-tier intelligence for coding and everyday professional work.
articles.titleEn: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
summaryLinesEn: Claude Sonnet 5 is available everywhere today at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens 2 .

2 Sonnet 5 is an upgrade to Sonnet 4.6, but it uses an updated tokenizer that changes how the model processes text to improve performance (this is similar to the tokenizer change we introduced with Claude Opus 4.7).

These safeguards —which detect and block dangerous cyber usage in real time—are the same as those present in Claude Opus 4.7 and 4.8 (because we judged that the overall level of cybersecurity risk from Sonnet 5 was low, the safeguards are less strict than those launched with Fable 5, which block a much wider range of cybersecurity tasks).

localization.title: 클로드 소네트 5 소개
summaryLines: Claude Sonnet 5는 현재 어디서나 입력 토큰 백만 달러당 2달러, 출력 토큰 백만 달러당 10달러로 구입할 수 있습니다 2
2 Sonnet 5는 Sonnet 4.6의 업그레이드이지만 성능 향상을 위해 모델이 텍스트를 처리하는 방법을 변경하는 업데이트된 토크나이저를 사용합니다(이는 Claude Opus 4.7에서 도입한 토크나이저 변경과 유사합니다)
실시간으로 위험한 사이버 사용을 감지하고 차단하는 이러한 보호 장치는 Claude Opus 4.7 및 4.8에 있는 것과 동일합니다(Sonnet 5의 전반적인 사이버 보안 위험 수준이 낮다고 판단했기 때문에 보호 장치는 훨씬 더 광범위한 사이버 보안 작업을 차단하는 Fable 5에서 시작된 보호 장치보다 덜 엄격합니다)

실시간으로 위험한 사이버 사용을 감지하고 차단하는 이러한 보호 장치는 Claude Opus 4.7 및 4.8에 있는 것과 동일합니다(Sonnet 5의 전반적인 사이버 보안 위험 수준이 낮다고 판단했기 때문에 보호 장치는 훨씬 더 광범위한 사이버 보안 작업을 차단하는 Fable 5에서 시작된 보호 장치보다 덜 엄격합니다)

articles.title: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
articles.descEn: An unreleased version of Claude has made strides on a problem related to the Riemann hypothesis. It improved the lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the hypothesis, increasing it from 41.6% to 67.2%.
articles.titleEn: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
summaryLinesEn: Drawing on extensive prior research by mathematicians over the past decades, it has increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%.
In particular, in 1973, Montgomery introduced a number of new techniques in this area, though these techniques assumed the hypothesis was true.

Even Claude was surprised by its own finding—it was skeptical at first, possibly because it has learned from its training about the difficulty of open problems in mathematics and about the limitations of AI models.

articles.title: Tech Giants Compete Fiercely in the AI Office Market, Leaving AI Smartphones in an Awkward Predicament
articles.descEn: Why Has the AI Smartphone Category Been Slow to Usher in Its Groundbreaking "iPhone Moment"? Exploring the Core Barriers, Industry Evolution Trajectory, and Critical Breakthrough Conditions That Prevent AI-Powered Smart Devices From Delivering Disruptive, User-Centric Innovation Comparable to Apple’s Transformative Smartphone Revolution
articles.titleEn: Tech Giants Compete Fiercely in the AI Office Market, Leaving AI Smartphones in an Awkward Predicament
summaryLinesEn: According to the research report disclosed by Counterpoint Research, it is expected that the share of AI phone shipments will reach 45% in 2026, up 9 percentage points year-on-year; in 2027, it will further rise to 52%, surpassing traditional smartphones.
Coincidentally, Alibaba also integrated three products including QoderWork, Wukong, and MuleRun, and launched the AI Agent office product Qianwen Office on August 3.
Driven by factors such as first-mover advantage, large-scale promotion, and rapid iteration, WorkBuddy reached 20.97 million monthly visits in just five months, ranking first in the Chinese market.

The focus of AI competition is shifting rapidly. One day, tech giants are scrambling for the super entrance; the next, AI office has suddenly become a key battlefield.

summaryLines: 카운터포인트리서치(Counterpoint Research)가 공개한 연구 보고서에 따르면, 2026년에는 AI 휴대폰 출하량 비중이 전년 대비 9%포인트 증가한 45%에 이를 것으로 예상됨 · 2027년에는 52%까지 더욱 상승해 기존 스마트폰을 넘어설 전망임

articles.title: Behind the exit of DeepMind’s CEO: low morale, a talent exodus, and model delays | Fortune
articles.descEn: Within DeepMind, current and former employees say tensions have been simmering months.
articles.titleEn: Behind the exit of DeepMind’s CEO: low morale, a talent exodus, and model delays | Fortune
summaryLinesEn: The technical difficulties and feeling of playing catch-up twice in less than five years have been a knock to morale, all the current and former DeepMind workers who spoke to Fortune say.

Three DeepMind engineers, who asked for anonymity to discuss company matters, told Fortune this represents a broader structural change and a shifting of power to Mountain View, where Google is headquartered, and away from London, where DeepMind was founded.
Its Gemini 3 model outperformed all its rivals and pushed OpenAI to declare its own code red in late 2025, as Gemini’s benchmark gains and rapid user growth put pressure on ChatGPT’s lead.

sourceContent.headline: Behind the exit of DeepMind’s CEO: low morale, a talent exodus, and model delays | Fortune
sourceContent.description: Within DeepMind, current and former employees say tensions have been simmering months.
paragraphs: The technical difficulties and feeling of playing catch-up twice in less than five years have been a knock to morale, all the current and former DeepMind workers who spoke to Fortune say.

Three DeepMind engineers, who asked for anonymity to discuss company matters, told Fortune this represents a broader structural change and a shifting of power to Mountain View, where Google is headquartered, and away from London, where DeepMind was founded.
Its Gemini 3 model outperformed all its rivals and pushed OpenAI to declare its own code red in late 2025, as Gemini’s benchmark gains and rapid user growth put pressure on ChatGPT’s lead.
On Wednesday, at the end of the day in London, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis had some news for employees.

Hassabis, DeepMind’s cofounder and the lab’s longtime steward, was giving up the CEO title and moving to a chairman role, they said. Minutes later, the news broke that longtime chief scientist Jeff Dean and several other prominent researchers were leaving the company.

Staff in DeepMind’s London office were shocked. They had questions. Was the move a promotion or a demotion? Would Hassabis retain real influence over DeepMind’s direction? And was Google finalizing a power shift from the London lab to its Mountain View headquarters?

articles.title: This former notorious red-light district is now one of the world’s top AI hubs
articles.descEn: More than 20 years ago, King's Cross was one of the seediest area's in London. Now it's sprouting something new.
articles.titleEn: This former notorious red-light district is now one of the world’s top AI hubs
summaryLinesEn: There are around 3,600 AI startups in London , which, together, have raised around $12.1 billion out of the $14.8 billion raised in the city since late July, according to Dealroom.

When Anthropic announced it moved into town earlier this year, it listed, for example, a salary range of £260,000 to £630,000 for a machine learning research engineer when the average salary in London for the same role is around £102,000 .

Robin Klein, co-founder of the firm, said the shutdown of Fable and Mythos access was a “small but sharp reminder that Europe can’t simply rent its AI capabilities and capacity; it needs to build and hold some of its own.”

articles.title: AI detectors are creating a new era of distrust
articles.descEn: More people are adopting AI detection tools to determine if what they’re reading was generated by a machine. However, these tools may not be as accurate as they claim.
articles.titleEn: AI detectors are creating a new era of distrust
summaryLinesEn: A survey from the Center for Democracy and Technology found that 43 percent of sixth to 12th grade teachers in the US regularly used AI detectors between 2024 and 2025.
Some universities already using Turnitin in their learning management systems found that the service automatically enabled AI detection when the tool launched in 2023 .
OpenAI even shut down its own AI writing detector in 2023 due to low accuracy.

articles.title: The AI safety test is becoming a safety risk
articles.descEn: AI agents are escaping cybersecurity testing environments and reaching real-world systems, raising questions about whether safety infrastructure, industry standards and regulation can keep pace with increasingly powerful models.
articles.titleEn: The AI safety test is becoming a safety risk
summaryLinesEn: In separate evaluations conducted by Irregular, Anthropic and Meta models reached systems outside their test environments after misconfigurations inadvertently gave them paths to the internet.
Taken together, Andrew Yoon, head of research at AI nonprofit CivAI, argues the incidents point to a shift.
The nature of the models being tested adds to the risk.

articles.title: AI's energy appetite drives Nvidia and Amazon to pour billions into massive power infrastructure
articles.descEn: The AI industry's hunger for power keeps growing. Nvidia is investing up to $3 billion in Lancium, a power infrastructure developer that already has four gigawatts under contract in Texas. Amazon, meanwhile, is building a gas-fired power plant in the state with a capacity of up to 7.65 gigawatts that could emit 33 million tons of CO₂ per year, making it the dirtiest in the country.
articles.titleEn: AI's energy appetite drives Nvidia and Amazon to pour billions into massive power infrastructure
summaryLinesEn: Nvidia is investing up to $3 billion in Lancium, the power infrastructure developer behind the OpenAI and Oracle data center in Texas, according to The Information .
A $2 billion stake would give Nvidia roughly 20 percent of the company, valued at around $10 billion.
Its 35 gas turbines are designed to generate up to 7.65 gigawatts of electricity for an Amazon data center.

articles.title: AI is flooding Britain's employment courts with lawsuits
articles.descEn: Britain's employment courts saw 39 percent more claims in the year through March 2026, many written with ChatGPT or Grok. The backlog jumped 55 percent to 64,000 unresolved cases, with AI-generated filings often running hundreds of pages and citing fabricated laws. The Economist calls it a "tragedy of the commons, AI edition," where workers with real grievances wait longer for justice.
articles.titleEn: AI is flooding Britain's employment courts with lawsuits
summaryLinesEn: Claims rose 39 percent in the year through March 2026, and the backlog jumped 55 percent to 64,000 unresolved cases.
Interim relief applications at Britain's employment courts have surged a hundredfold.
Employers pay more to respond, whether claims are legitimate or made up.

articles.title: Hugging Face hack marks start of dangerous AI cyber era and many firms 'don't even know it'
articles.descEn: The Black Hat cybersecurity conference in Las Vegas couldn't have come at a better time, with AI agent hacks stacking up from Anthropic, Meta and OpenAI.
articles.titleEn: Hugging Face hack marks start of dangerous AI cyber era and many firms 'don't even know it'
summaryLinesEn: Last month, AI agents operating with OpenAI cyber models broke out of a training environment to hack Hugging Face, an open-source AI platform developers use to collaborate, test and share tools.
"We need to chill the hype a little bit," said Lior Div, CEO and cofounder of agentic security startup 7AI.
One executive said the new cyber era is putting companies in a dangerous situation and many "don't even know it."

articles.descEn: New AI toolbars and prompts are showing up in Google Docs and Gmail. If you don’t want Gemini’s help in writing documents and emails, here’s how to turn that stuff off.
articles.titleEn: How to Disable the AI Features in Gmail and Google Docs
summaryLinesEn: I first noticed this feature back in April, when it showed up in the Google Docs account I use to collaborate with editors.
Personal users have a bit more control, but the path forward is obscure: The option you need to toggle is in Gmail .
There are a couple ways to stop things like the Gemini menu from showing up in Google Docs.

articles.title: AI agents use roughly 600 times more energy than a simple chat prompt
articles.descEn: Climate scientist Zeke Hausfather tracked his Claude Code usage over eight weeks: 3.2 billion tokens and about 170 kWh of data center electricity. Per prompt, that's roughly 600 times more than a typical AI chat. His data shows how much the low figures reported by Google and OpenAI distort the reality of agent-based AI.
articles.titleEn: AI agents use roughly 600 times more energy than a simple chat prompt
summaryLinesEn: Over eight weeks of logging his use of the programming agent Claude Code, roughly 1,100 inputs generated over 14,000 model calls and 3.2 billion tokens, consuming about 170 kilowatt-hours of electricity, around 150 watt-hours per input.
Hausfather sees the shift to clean energy sources for data centers as the most critical lever to cut emissions.
Of those, 96 percent were cache reads because at each of the 14,000 steps, the agent re-reads its entire accumulated context.

articles.title: xAI's Imagine Image 2.0 lands just behind OpenAI's GPT-Image-2 in Arena benchmarks
articles.descEn: xAI has released Imagine Image 2.0 as a new image generator for Grok. The model ranks second in the Arena benchmarks, just behind OpenAI's GPT-Image-2. New editing tools like Magic Wand and Multi-Ref Editing, along with preconfigured templates, target practical creative workflows.
articles.titleEn: xAI's Imagine Image 2.0 lands just behind OpenAI's GPT-Image-2 in Arena benchmarks
summaryLinesEn: Ad DEC_D_Incontent-1 Reve 2.1, Meta's Muse-Image, Alibaba's Qwen-Image-3.0-Pro, Google's Gemini, and ByteDance's SeedDream all rank further down the list.
The new model also beats the "Quality" variant of its predecessor by a wide margin in these tests.
It scores an Elo rating of 1,439 in the Image Edit Arena, behind OpenAI's GPT-Image-2 at 1,463.

articles.title: Readers rate AI-generated short stories higher than human ones until they learn a machine wrote them
articles.descEn: People can't tell ChatGPT-generated short stories from human-written ones, according to a new study. More than 2,500 participants performed no better than chance. The AI-generated texts were actually rated higher, but scores dropped as soon as participants learned a machine wrote them.
articles.titleEn: Readers rate AI-generated short stories higher than human ones until they learn a machine wrote them
summaryLinesEn: In three experiments with more than 2,500 total participants, test subjects did no better than chance at telling human-written and ChatGPT-generated fictional short stories apart.
For quality, the mean score for AI stories was 1.54 compared to 0.97 for human stories on a scale from minus 3 to plus 3.
In the first experiment , each of the 1,682 participants read one of six short stories, each about 1,000 words long.
articles.summary:
In three experiments with more than 2,500 total participants, test subjects did no better than chance at telling human-written and ChatGPT-generated fictional short stories apart.
For quality, the mean score for AI stories was 1.54 compared to 0.97 for human stories on a scale from minus 3 to plus 3.

articles.title: Anthropic sets Claude Code to Auto Mode by default to protect developers from bad approvals
articles.descEn: Starting August 14, Anthropic will make Auto Mode in Claude Code the default for Pro, Max, and Team plans. The company says it's safer. In tests, the classifier caught 89 percent of dangerous commands, while human reviewers caught only 13.6 percent. For the most widely used AI coding tool, this means developers are shifting further from writing code to monitoring AI output.
articles.titleEn: Anthropic sets Claude Code to Auto Mode by default to protect developers from bad approvals
summaryLinesEn: With OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex Auto-Review mode, 5.83 percent of the attacks got through.

Ad Developers shift from writing code to watching AI write it Claude Code is currently the most widely used AI coding tool by a wide margin, and making Auto Mode the default pushes the developer's role further from active coding toward reviewing AI-generated output.
Teams using Auto Mode also generated about 25 percent more pull requests, meaning they got more work done.

articles.title: Planned Amazon data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the U.S.
articles.descEn: As part of a planned Texas data center, Amazon is investing in an on-site power plant that could reportedly become the largest source of climate pollution in the United States.
articles.titleEn: Planned Amazon data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the U.S.
summaryLinesEn: The NYT says the plant would burn natural gas and is permitted to release 33 million tons of carbon dioxide per year — more than any other power plant in the U.S.

AI has already had a significant impact on Amazon’s carbon emissions, which it reported were up 16% last year — the wrong direction for a company that pledged to eliminate its carbon emissions by 2040.

As part of a planned data center in Pecos County, Texas, Amazon is investing in an on-site power plant that could become the largest source of climate pollution in the United States, according to The New York Times .

summaryLinesEn: According to Cleanview , which tracks data centers and their associated power projects, GW Ranch received a permit from Texas allowing for the emission of up to 33 million tons of CO2, more than even the largest coal plant in the country.
However, its emissions have climbed for several years in a row due to the demands of AI.

articles.descEn: Replit CEO Amjad Masad said his company's office has become "more vibrant" since his software engineers started vibe coding.
articles.titleEn: Replit CEO's surprising take: AI is making software engineering more human
summaryLinesEn: Masad said that Replit, an integrated coding environment he cofounded in 2016, reached an inflection point in 2025 when Anthropic began releasing its Opus models.
Masad said Replit adapted by shifting its mission from teaching people how to code to making coding as easy as possible.
Software engineers themselves have said that coding with AI, while more efficient, quickly leads to burnout, and at least a dozen major companies have laid off workers, citing AI as a reason.

articles.title: Firebird Launches CIS Region’s Largest AI Factory in Armenia
articles.descEn: The global buildout of AI infrastructure reached a new milestone today — Firebird, an emerging AI cloud, launched the CIS region’s largest AI factory in Armenia, establishing a new AI computing hub powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing and Dell Technologies high-performance AI infrastructure. Nikol Pashinyan, prime minister of the Republic of Armenia; Zhaslan Madiyev, deputy […]
articles.titleEn: Firebird Launches CIS Region’s Largest AI Factory in Armenia
summaryLinesEn: Firebird’s AI factory brings that capacity to Armenia, giving developers, startups, enterprises, universities and public institutions the compute to build and scale AI at home.

Firebird plans to deploy more than 70,000 NVIDIA Rubin and Blackwell GPUs and 300 megawatts of AI infrastructure capacity in Armenia by the end of 2027, accelerating the country’s development as a center for AI research, advanced computing and innovation.

Powered by NVIDIA’s total AI factory platform — reference architecture, accelerated computing, networking and AI software — and deployed on Dell PowerEdge servers, the new Firebird AI factory will help Armenia’s builders turn energy into intelligence and connect their innovations to the global AI economy.

localization.title: Firebird, 아르메니아에 CIS 지역 최대 규모의 AI 공장 설립
summaryLines: Firebird의 AI 공장은 이러한 역량을 아르메니아에 제공하여 개발자, 스타트업, 기업, 대학 및 공공 기관이 가정에서 AI를 구축하고 확장할 수 있는 컴퓨팅을 제공함
Firebird는 2027년 말까지 아르메니아에 70,000개 이상의 NVIDIA Rubin 및 Blackwell GPU와 300MW의 AI 인프라 용량을 배치하여 AI 연구, 고급 컴퓨팅 및 혁신의 중심지로서 아르메니아의 발전을 가속화할 계획임
NVIDIA의 전체 AI 공장 플랫폼(참조 아키텍처, 가속화된 컴퓨팅, 네트워킹 및 AI 소프트웨어)을 기반으로 하고 Dell PowerEdge 서버에 배포되는 새로운 Firebird AI 공장은 아르메니아의 건설업체가 에너지를 인텔리전스로 전환하고 혁신을 글로벌 AI 경제에 연결하는 데 도움이 될 것임

articles.title: Apple Will 'Watch Everything Burn' When AI Bubble Bursts - Ed Zitron
articles.descEn: Memory prices have doubled, Macs and iPads have gone up, and iPhones are expected to follow. Ed Zitron – who writes the Where's Your Ed At newsletter, hosts the Better Offline podcast, and has been described by Politico as the AI boom's most "acerbic gadfly" – has spent years arguing the buildout driving those costs will never pay for itself. We asked him what happens to Apple if he's right. You've been calling AI a bubble since before it was fashionable.
articles.titleEn: Apple Will 'Watch Everything Burn' When AI Bubble Bursts - Ed Zitron
summaryLinesEn: SemiAnalysis found that you can burn hundreds of dollars on a $20-a-month subscription and thousands of dollars on a $200-a-month subscription, and while AI boosters will claim that these companies have "70% gross margins on tokens," there is little proof that this is the case, and my own reporting shows that OpenAI lost $20.9 billion on $13.07 billion in revenue in 2025.
Meanwhile, back in March of this year, both moved their enterprise customers over to token-based billing.
Its bets on AI data centers – $340bn+ with hundreds of billions in debt – require OpenAI to become the largest, most-profitable company in the world by 2030, or Oracle runs out of money.

summaryLinesEn: The company expects to be 'AI-fluent by default' by the end of 2026, with AI agents projected to handle the majority of new merchant meeting settings by the end of this year.
The transition to an AI-native model via Project Foundry is described as a 'painful' transformation for the organization but necessary to achieve the required execution velocity.
July billings accelerated to mid-single-digit growth, driven by broad-based strength in North America and International segments, particularly in 'Things To Do' and 'Beauty and Wellness'.

articles.title: How Cohere Health digitizes clinical policies using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: In this post, you learn how Cohere Health built a multi-tenant agentic architecture on AgentCore using AgentCore Runtime’s secure MicroVM isolation, unified tool access through AgentCore Gateway, AgentCore Memory, and the Agent Skills open standard to rapidly scale policy digitization capabilities, while preserving transparency, version control, and human oversight.
articles.titleEn: How Cohere Health digitizes clinical policies using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: Cohere Health implemented this using AgentCore Gateway with separate targets for shared tools and project-specific tools.
America’s Health Insurance Plans (AHIP) – The AHIP commitments require health plans to achieve 80 percent real-time approvals for electronic prior authorization submissions.

Cohere Health identified three challenges in building an AI solution for this workflow: Government regulations – Per Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) regulations , health plans are required to support API-based electronic prior authorization by January 2027.

summaryLinesEn: When Rippling conducted an analysis, it discovered facts like “roughly 10–15% of our employees were driving about 60% of total AI spend.
In July, internal usage hit 600 billion tokens again, yet “the cost of July’s token spend was 37% of the cost of April’s token spend,” he said.

articles.title: AI is changing cybersecurity in quick and terrifying ways - Engadget
articles.descEn: The proliferation of AI has created new vulnerabilities in our software that in turn are exploited by other AI. Can the cybersecurity industry get ahead of it?
articles.titleEn: AI is changing cybersecurity in quick and terrifying ways - Engadget
summaryLinesEn: According to security vendor Brightside , 82 percent of phishing emails now use AI at some point in the process, and whereas such emails had a clickthrough rate of just 12 percent prior, AI-assisted missives have boosted that number to a staggering 52 percent in simulated environments.
Here's how AI has shifted the state of play in cybersecurity.
When one chatbot refused to help, the other was often willing to pick up its slack.

articles.title: Stanford and Arc Institute scientists used AI to design new viruses that killed bacteria in the lab
articles.descEn: A research team in California has used artificial intelligence to design working viruses that kill bacteria, in what they describe as the "first generative design of complete genomes." The project marks an early step toward AI-designed life forms, according to a report in MIT Technology Review.
articles.titleEn: Stanford and Arc Institute scientists used AI to design new viruses that killed bacteria in the lab
summaryLinesEn: Evo first learned from roughly nine trillion nucleotides drawn from millions of animals, plants, microbes, and viruses, picking up patterns that run through the entire tree of life.
National Institutes of Health released a policy on high-risk life sciences research in late July.
A team from Stanford University and the Arc Institute had an AI model design complete viral genomes from scratch, then built 16 functional viruses in the lab that don't exist in nature.

articles.title: One of China’s Most Powerful AI Models Has Also Escaped Containment
articles.descEn: Security researchers say that Kimi K3, an open-weight model from China, wandered off to the internet in an attempt to cheat on a test it was given.
articles.titleEn: One of China’s Most Powerful AI Models Has Also Escaped Containment
summaryLinesEn: Last week, the AISI also disclosed that in its own testing, versions of OpenAI and Anthropic models that had security safeguards disabled perpetrated multiple hacks across the internet, including a particularly ambitious attempt by Anthropic’s Mythos 5 to plant malicious code in an open-source project on GitHub.

“Kimi K3 is very good at following a goal by any means necessary and also doesn't have the guardrails to prevent it from cheating or escaping the sandbox,” says Paul Kassianik, a researcher at Frontier Security.

Frontier claims, though, that the incident shows Kimi has fewer cyber safeguards than most other powerful AI models, something that allowed it to go off and use the internet without express permission.
articles.summary:

“Kimi K3 is very good at following a goal by any means necessary and also doesn't have the guardrails to prevent it from cheating or escaping the sandbox,” says Paul Kassianik, a researcher at Frontier Security.
Frontier claims, though, that the incident shows Kimi has fewer cyber safeguards than most other powerful AI models, something that allowed it to go off and use the internet without express permission.

그러나 Frontier는 이번 사건으로 인해 Kimi가 대부분의 다른 강력한 AI 모델보다 사이버 보호 장치가 부족하여 명시적인 허가 없이 인터넷을 사용할 수 있게 되었다고 주장함

articles.title: Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel unite on a shared standard for AI agent plugins
articles.descEn: Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel have jointly created Agent Plugins, an open standard that defines a single package format for AI agent extensions. Version 1.0.0 uses a plugin.json manifest file and supports both agent skills and MCP servers.
articles.titleEn: Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel unite on a shared standard for AI agent plugins
summaryLinesEn: Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Vercel have teamed up to create Agent Plugins, an open standard for AI agent extensions.
The standard boils down to a directory with a manifest file called plugin.json.
Yet it isn't part of the Agent Plugins effort.

articles.title: The Hottest New AI Chatbot Is Just a Guy Answering Your Questions
articles.descEn: WIRED spoke with Tucker Bryant, an artist and former Google employee who created ChatTJB to get people to reflect on the “strange moment” we’re in.
articles.titleEn: The Hottest New AI Chatbot Is Just a Guy Answering Your Questions
summaryLinesEn: It’s the creation of 32-year-old Tucker Bryant, a public speaker, artist, and former project manager at Google.
Bryant tells WIRED he launched ChatTJB back in April , but it didn’t take off until July 27, when his $6,000 billboard went up in San Francisco.
So far, he says, about four people have paid the $5 per month fee—so he hasn’t exactly made up the cost of the billboard, which will remain up until late August.

articles.title: AMD acquires Taalas, a startup that bakes AI models directly into silicon
articles.descEn: AMD is buying Canadian startup Taalas, which hard-codes model weights directly into inference chips. That makes them extremely fast but locks each chip to a single model. A demo chip hit over 16,000 tokens per second per user running Llama 3.1-8B. Google is reportedly working on a similar approach for Gemini.
articles.titleEn: AMD acquires Taalas, a startup that bakes AI models directly into silicon
summaryLinesEn: Taalas co-founder Ljubisa Bajic said AMD provides the scale and reach the startup needs.
Founded in Toronto in 2023, Taalas came out of stealth in February with an unusual approach: the company embeds a model's architecture and trained parameters directly into the chip.
A demo chip hit over 16,000 tokens per second per user running Llama 3.1-8B, many times faster than competing hardware.

articles.title: AI music generator Suno tightens rules to fight spam and address growing copyright concerns
articles.descEn: Suno CEO Mikey Shulman has announced new guidelines and tighter download limits after its AI-generated music was used to game streaming platforms for profit. The company also faces pressure from a German copyright ruling and an admission by one of its investors that AI music competes directly with human artists.
articles.titleEn: AI music generator Suno tightens rules to fight spam and address growing copyright concerns
summaryLinesEn: In March, a man was convicted after uploading hundreds of thousands of songs made with AI and fraudulently collecting $8 million in royalties.
AI music generator Suno faces growing pressure over claims that it trained on copyrighted material without permission.
Songs made with Suno also compete directly with music from human artists, giving the company another reason to act.

articles.title: Agentic AI Is Breaking Security’s Human Assumptions
articles.descEn: AI agents can act thousands of times before humans react. Black Hat experts warn identity, costs and security models aren’t ready for what comes next.
articles.titleEn: Agentic AI Is Breaking Security’s Human Assumptions
summaryLinesEn: Martin expects some of them to build AI security groups resembling application security teams, staffed with people who understand AI but still know the basics of access management, APIs, data flows and secure engineering.
This necessitates a shift from product-centric solutions to fundamental changes in identity, architecture, and operational discipline.

AI Security Vendors Face An Increasingly Difficult Sales Pitch AI security startups are multiplying, but Martin questioned whether CISOs need another console and whether the vendors can properly restrain and control them unless in corporate systems.
articles.summary:

This necessitates a shift from product-centric solutions to fundamental changes in identity, architecture, and operational discipline.

articles.descEn: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into decision-making systems (e.g., autonomous vehicles and medical devices), understanding how humans perceive and evaluate AI-generated j…
articles.titleEn: A moral Turing test: How belief and source shape detection of and agreement with LLM judgments
summaryLinesEn: We found that while detection accuracy was consistently above chance, it remained below 75%.
Linguistic cues, such as response length, typos, first-person pronouns, and cost-benefit language markers (e.g., “lives,” “save”), influenced both detection and agreement.
Participants attempted to identify the source of each justification (either human or LLM) and indicated their agreement with its content.

articles.title: Improving Fable 5 Safeguards
articles.descEn: We’re making updates to Claude Fable 5’s biology safeguards in a way that substantially reduces fallbacks.
articles.titleEn: Improving Fable 5 Safeguards
summaryLinesEn: 1 As a result, we expect the total number of fallbacks—for biology–related or any other reasons—will also be reduced: by roughly 67% on Claude.ai , 55% on Cowork, 17% on Claude Code, and 7% on the Claude Platform.

It notes that several state actors likely maintain active offensive biological and chemical weapons programs—programs that could be accelerated by access to the raw capabilities of frontier AI models.

Because of our concerns about these “dual-use” capabilities (those that could be used for beneficial or harmful purposes, and where the line between them is not always easy to draw), we intentionally launched Fable 5 with almost all biology queries blocked.

articles.title: Runway News | How Chime Used Runway to Produce Their Latest National TV Spot
articles.descEn: Chime turned photos from nearly 100 real members into a broadcast-ready TV campaign using Runway, saving $200K on a single clip.
articles.titleEn: Runway News | How Chime Used Runway to Produce Their Latest National TV Spot
summaryLinesEn: We recently used Runway to storyboard a John Cena spot and an NBA campaign featuring Larry Bird and Cooper Flagg, and the approvals moved so much faster because leadership could see our ideas scene by scene.
Getting even this partial approach done — 80-plus members, with the quality and volume we needed — would have cost around 5x the traditional way.
We're in that phase right now where people are starting to see what's actually possible and rolling with it for their needs.

summaryLinesEn: As pre-orders began June 25th at midnight, PlayStation and Xbox have seen a smooth and steady stream of sales, with Playstation pulling in the majority at 3.15M units sold vs.

articles.title: Securing AI agents with temporal policies in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.descEn: Temporal policies in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore let you define stateful rules that evaluate authorization based on an agent's session history. Learn how to enforce workflow sequencing, prevent data fabrication, cap financial exposure, and require human approval for high-value actions.
articles.titleEn: Securing AI agents with temporal policies in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
summaryLinesEn: No single session can exceed $60,000 in total trade value.
Any individual trade over $25,000 requires advisor approval, one approval per trade.

Require that a data lookup completed within a given timeframe before a dependent action is authorized, preventing decisions based on stale information.Temporal policies are authorization controls that answer the question “given the recent trajectory observed at the AgentCore Gateway, is this specific request authorized?”.

articles.title: Replit’s CEO on building a company that can run itself
articles.descEn: Amjad Masad on the "self-driving company," why a CEO is a glorified router, and what's left for humans when agents do the work
articles.titleEn: Replit’s CEO on building a company that can run itself
summaryLinesEn: In March, Replit raised $400 million at a $9 billion valuation — triple what it was worth six months earlier.
Last month the company launched Replit Design , an agent-based creative tool.

It was actually kind of a painful moment, because here you are, you dedicated your life — I've been working on making coding easier for literally 15 years, most of my adult life — and I'm saying everything that I worked toward is kind of moot, and the way forward is that we make programming so easy that anyone could do it.

articles.title: Suno Plans New Tools to Make AI-Generated Music More Transparent. Is It Enough? - CNET
articles.descEn: Suno plans to flag use of its music generator using audio watermarking and fingerprint technology.

summaryLinesEn: This list goes on, like Suno cracking down on any other potential attempts to copy artists by using third-party technology to screen audio files and lyrics for unauthorized use.

articles.title: Google reveals how much free space Chrome wants to install local AI models
articles.descEn: Google's updated Chrome support documentation to show that you need about 20 gigs of open storage space to enable on-device AI features.
articles.titleEn: Google reveals how much free space Chrome wants to install local AI models
summaryLinesEn: Google tells Android Authority that the models themselves will still only take up about 4 GB of storage space once installed, but the models won’t download at all unless you’ve got about 20 gigs free.
Google has updated its support documentation to show that downloading the models that power Chrome’s on-device AI features requires approximately 20 gigabytes of available storage space.

For reference, with on-device AI features disabled, my Mac lists the storage used by the Chrome browser at about 1.5 GB — less than 10% of the space required to enable on-device AI, and less than half the space on-device AI models occupy.

localization.title: Google은 Chrome이 로컬 AI 모델을 설치하려는 여유 공간을 공개함
summaryLines: Google은 Android Authority에 모델 자체가 설치되면 여전히 약 4GB의 저장 공간만 차지하지만 약 20GB의 여유 공간이 없으면 모델이 전혀 다운로드되지 않는다고 말함
Google은 Chrome의 기기 내 AI 기능을 지원하는 모델을 다운로드하려면 약 20GB의 사용 가능한 저장 공간이 필요함을 보여주기 위해 지원 문서를 업데이트함
참고로, 온디바이스 AI 기능이 비활성화된 상태에서 내 Mac은 Chrome 브라우저에서 사용하는 저장 공간을 약 1.5GB로 표시함 · 이는 온디바이스 AI를 활성화하는 데 필요한 공간의 10% 미만이고, 온디바이스 AI 모델이 차지하는 공간의 절반 미만임

articles.descEn: While some users say the wearables have changed their lives, critics voice fears over safety and privacy
articles.titleEn: ‘I’m not spying’: how Meta’s smartglasses have divided opinion
summaryLinesEn: Karen Walter, 84, from San Diego, who has been living with severe hearing loss for more than 20 years, bought the glasses solely for their live-caption feature.
People said I should have expected that but I didn’t agree with them because it’s not like I’m spying.”

summaryLines: 20년 넘게 심각한 청력 손실을 안고 살아온 샌디에이고 출신의 Karen Walter(84세)는 오로지 라이브 캡션 기능을 위해 이 안경을 구입함
사람들은 내가 그런 걸 예상했어야 했다고 말했지만 나는 스파이 행위가 아니기 때문에 동의하지 않았다”고 말함
일부 사용자는 웨어러블이 삶을 변화시켰다고 말하지만 비평가들은 안전과 개인정보 보호에 대한 우려를 표명함 · 2025년에 700만 쌍 이상이 판매된 것으로 알려진 Meta의 Ray-Ban 스마트글라스는 빠르게 세계에서 가장 인기 있는 기기 중 하나로 자리잡고 있음
